content:
What's your best advice to getting a firm hold on the basics of Lean? For reference I am a MS student at Stanford and really want to understand how to both use lean and how it works under the hood. (My gut tells me to learn the basics of how to use lean with tactics before lifting up the hood and learning how it actually works)

I have gone through all of the NNG and about halfway through the analysis course as well. Feeling mostly competent there after a day, I started moving towards MIL, and it seems like the ground has shifted from underneath me a bit. Before I invest more time into this text, is this the recommended path forward?

For reference, what I don't have:

  • I don't know much type theory
  • almost no knowledge of lambda calculus
  • no experience with formal verification

What I do have:

  • I do have a strong/rigorous applied math background.
  • plenty of programming experience
  • a lot of curiosity.
  • A strong ability to learn things from self-directed study.

How do you guys recommend going forward?

What are you struggling with when it comes to mil? The idea of it is precisely to get you to the point of proving interesting things without having to go through too much of the type theory aspects (hardly any in fact)
Personally, I always recommend giving #tpil a quick read as well.
You can also have a look at the talks registered on our channel, for example here
